text: Corporate Liability in Autonomous Systems: Intersecting Corporate Ethics with Transnational Tech Governance - An Indonesia Perspective on Cross-Border Algorithmic Accountability and Legal Risk Mitigation presents the following source proposition: The rapid proliferation of high-level Autonomous Systems (AS) has generated unprecedented systemic risks, exposing a profound accountability gap within classical jurisprudence. This proposition is pertinent to Kaal's source-bound claim that German commentators, whose expertise German courts rely on heavily, concluded after the financial crisis that managers do not act reasonably under the German business judgment rule if the risks they take on behalf of the corporation result in the demise of the corporation. The proposed response is an extension: the relationship should remain limited to the retrieved source proposition and the mapped Kaal claim unless fuller source review supports a broader conclusion.
